newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine o/night money steady, termed rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Philippine o/night money steady, termed rates fall.

text.p: * Bankers locking in funds in long-termed issues

Philippine overnight money remained steady at 10.84375 percent, hovering just above the Central Bank's borrowing rate of 10.75 percent, as banks shifted their investible funds to longer-termed issues, traders said.
Termed instruments were actively traded as some banks tried to lock in their funds before rates go down further, while others tried to post trading gains in time for the year-end book closing.

Turnover in the interbank call loan market was anaemic with only 14.451 billion pesos changing hands among 21 lenders and 30 borrowers. Done rates were bound between 10.78125 percent and 11.125 percent.

Interest rates on three-, six- and 12-month bills fell signficantly on Monday due to oversubscription. The system was awash with cash after the Central Bank suspended the weekly auction last week due to the APEC meeting.
"Maturing reverse repos and T-notes were also not rolled over because the Central Bank closed its repo window during the APEC period," one trader added.
The rarely-traded two-year fixed rate notes were being bought with effective rates going down to 12.85 percent to 13.0 percent, compared to their coupon of 13.75 percent.
Secondary rates for three-month bills also went down, with bids ranging from 11.5 to 11.65 percent and offers between 11.35 to 11.45 percent.
Six-month bills were being bid at 11.8 to 12.0 percent, and offered at 11.7 to 11.9 percent.
One-year bills were being bid at 12.10 to 12.5 percent and offered at 12.0 to 12.4 percent.
